guideTitle: The Best CPU Stands for Lifting a PC Off the Floor
metaTitle: Best CPU Floor Stands: Low Rolling Stands and Carts (2026)
metaDescription: We compared low CPU floor stands and one desk-height cart on lift height, size range, casters and price, from a $14 stand to the ZUAVIALA cart.
introParagraphs: A CPU floor stand raises a desktop tower an inch or two off the floor, which keeps carpet fibers and dust away from bottom intake vents and makes it easier to roll the PC out to reach cables. Most here are low, adjustable-width stands on casters costing under $20.

The differences are small but practical: lift height, whether the listing states a size range, and whether the wheels lock. One product, the ZUAVIALA, is a taller cart that raises the tower to near desk height instead.
None of these listings state a weight capacity. Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-1.summary: A ZUAVIALA metal cart adjustable from 21.34 to 28.3 inches high.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-1.description:
The ZUAVIALA is different from the other stands: a metal cart that raises the tower to 21.34–28.3 inches, near desk height, and adds surface space.

It costs about $41 at the time of writing, far more than the low stands. Choose it if you want the tower within reach rather than just off the floor.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-1.bestFor: Keeping the PC beside the desk at reach height.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-1.skipIf: You only want the tower off the floor; a $15 stand does that.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-2.summary: A Hmseng adjustable-width stand with an open bottom, 2 inches off the floor.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-2.description:
The Hmseng raises the tower 2 inches, the most lift listed among the low stands, with an open bottom that Hmseng says helps cooling and reduces dust intake.

It has adjustable width and casters, for about $18 at the time of writing. The width range is not stated.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-2.bestFor: PCs with bottom intake vents on carpet.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-2.skipIf: You need a stated size range; the Liitrton lists one.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-3.summary: A Hovadova stand with four 360° casters that lock.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-3.description:
This Hovadova stand has locking casters to keep the PC in place once positioned, with tool-free setup, for about $17 at the time of writing.

The listing does not give a size range.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-3.bestFor: PCs that should not roll when bumped.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-3.skipIf: You need a stated size range.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-4.summary: An adjustable-width stand that lifts the PC 1.75 inches.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-4.description: This stand lifts the tower 1.75 inches with adjustable width and casters, for about $16 at the time of writing. The width range is not stated.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-4.skipIf: You want more lift; the Hmseng gives 2 inches.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-5.summary: A YOSE stand with almost no listed specifications.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-5.description: The YOSE is the cheapest stand here at about $14 at the time of writing, but its listing gives no size, lift or caster details. The Liitrton costs about a dollar more and states its dimensions.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-5.bestFor: Buyers who can check fit from photos.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-5.skipIf: You want stated dimensions; choose the Liitrton.

best-cpu-bottom-stands-6.summary: A Liitrton stand adjustable from 16.93 to 22.44 inches long, on 360° casters.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-6.description:
The Liitrton is the low stand with the clearest specifications: adjustable length from 16.93 to 22.44 inches and width from about 9 inches, on four 360-degree casters, for about $15 at the time of writing.

The long range suits most cases, including large towers. The lift height is not stated.
best-cpu-bottom-stands-6.skipIf: You want locking wheels; the Hovadova has them.

buyingCriteria.explanation: More clearance helps bottom intake vents. The Hmseng lists 2 inches; the carpet stand 1.75 inches.
Only the Liitrton states length and width ranges. Measure your case.
Locks keep the PC from rolling. The Hovadova lists them.
None of the listings state a capacity; confirm with the seller for heavy towers.

faq.q: Why raise a PC off the floor?
faq.a: It keeps carpet fibers and dust away from bottom vents and makes the PC easier to move for cleaning and cabling.

faq.q: How much lift do I need?
faq.a: An inch or two is typical. The Hmseng lists 2 inches.

faq.q: How much weight can these hold?
faq.a: None of the listings state a capacity. Check with the seller for a heavy tower.

bottomLine: For most towers, the Liitrton is the low stand with the clearest fit. The Hmseng gives the most lift for bottom vents, and the Hovadova adds locking wheels.
The ZUAVIALA is a different product, a desk-height cart, worth it only if you want the PC beside you. The YOSE is cheapest but lists too little to recommend confidently.
